notes.subject: Pay-per-play terms — historical guidance
notes.body: Important for future conversations with Carol O'Donnell / CS OktoberFest: Adventure Zone has used multiple pay-per-play structures historically, so do not promise one universal guarantee structure without Dave confirming the deal for this event. Examples found in 2026 Gmail history: (1) Mini Zone at no upfront cost with a $5,000 sales guarantee; after Adventure Zone reaches that sales amount, the event receives a percentage of ticket-box sales. (2) Hybrid structure where the event pays half the normal package price upfront, Adventure Zone charges the public, and after total receipts reach the normal package-price goal the event receives 10% of ticket-box sales. (3) In some cases Adventure Zone has offered no-upfront/no-guarantee pay-per-play with a percentage back to the event. Other 2026 emails confirm a 10% ticket-box share in some pay-per-play arrangements. Treat pay-per-play terms as event-specific and confirm any guarantee/minimum and percentage with Dave before quoting them as firm terms. Source: Adventure Zone Gmail history reviewed Aug. 27, 2026.
